class.name: ColorGradeVolume3D
class.brief_description: A [ColorGrade] for a place, a time of day or a weather.
class.description: Its [member grade] is blended into the camera's [Environment] (the camera's own, else the world's) while the camera is inside its box ([member size], centered on the node), fading in over [member blend_distance] as the camera comes in. A cave darker and colder, a market warmer, an underwater blue. A [member global] volume applies everywhere. [member when] makes it follow the day and the weather: a [constant WHEN_NIGHT] grade fades in as a [TimeOfDay] turns to night, a [constant WHEN_RAINING] one as a [Weather3D]'s rain starts, so the look of a stormy night is just two global volumes. Where volumes overlap, higher [member priority] goes over lower, each by how much it applies. [member weight] fades it by hand, for a flashback or a cutscene. The environment is given back as it was once the last volume goes. In the editor, it isn't touched.

method.name: get_influence
method.description: How much of its grade applies with the camera at [param camera] now, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code].

members.member: How far outside its box the grade starts fading in, in meters.
If [code]true[/code], it applies wherever the camera is, without a box.
Volumes of higher priority are blended over lower ones.
Its box, centered on the node and turned with it, in meters.
How much of its grade applies at most, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code].
When it applies: always, or as much as it's day, night, dawn or dusk ([TimeOfDay]'s), or overcast, raining or snowing ([Weather3D]'s).

constants.constant: While the sun is near the horizon, most when it's on it.
As much as a [Weather3D]'s sky is overcast.
As hard as a [Weather3D]'s rain falls.
As hard as a [Weather3D]'s snow falls.
